source: Statement Based Questions  01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 13; lecture example, exam/year not stated
statement: A mother tells her child, ‘If you bother me, I will slap you.’
items_I_II: The warning may make the child stop bothering her.
All children are naturally naughty.
question:
Statement: A mother tells her child, ‘If you bother me, I will slap you.’
Assumptions:
I. The warning may make the child stop bothering her.
II. All children are naturally naughty.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.C: Both assumptions I and II are implicit.
options.D: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit.

independent_reasoning: The warning is intended to deter the behaviour, so I is relied on. Nothing says all children are naughty; II is an unsupported generalisation.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
options.C: Only conclusion II follows.
options.D: Both conclusions I and II follow.

logical_outcome: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
independent_reasoning: The statement gives neither a specific month nor a country of residence. September is not established as winter from the supplied information, and Canada is unrelated.
